question: What kind of knowledge, when merely heard, must be sufficient to produce a result for one addressed as fair-faced?
premises: A means is stated as mere knowledge.
That knowledge is specified as heard knowledge.
It is addressed to one of fair face.
inference: Mere heard knowledge is presented as a sufficient means in this context.
uncertainties: Result of that means not specified here
plain_english: By this mere knowledge, by what has been heard, O fair-faced one.
